current_activity: controlling the landings from HQ in England

notes: About 60,000 First Army troops landed on Utah and Omaha on D-Day; army HQ (Bradley) controlled the landings from its England HQ at Bristol; under 21st Army Group. HQ moved ashore later (at Cricqueville-en-Bessin by 2 July per local source). Event definition: the landing is by First Army troops; the point is the army headquarters in England that controlled it, not the beaches (reviewed in the Batch 1 audit and kept deliberately).

current_activity: holding four-corps line from Cotentin to Caumont
notes: By 15 June four US corps in the line: V, XIX (operational 13 June), VIII (operational 15 June) and VII. Location is the centre of the southern front (not an HQ).
VII Corps captured Cherbourg (Schlieben surrendered 26 June, deputy Sattler 27 June; arsenal/harbour forts 29 June). Port heavily demolished.

current_activity: shifting weight south toward Saint-Lô front
notes: First Army shifts weight south: 79th Division moves under VIII Corps 28 June; 3rd Armored Division attack at Villiers-Fossard 29 June.

current_activity: launching Operation Cobra west of Saint-Lô with VII Corps in the lead
notes: Event date: Cobra opened 25 July (26 July was its second day, Breakout-13 p251). Event definition: the First Army offensive; VII Corps made the main effort. Location: Marigny marks the Cobra penetration sector, not General Bradley's First Army command post (Breakout-13/14). Opponents: engaged_with is not exhaustive. Breakout-13 describes Panzer Lehr (with a regiment of the 5th Parachute Division attached), elements of the 353rd Division and the 5th Parachute Division in the penetration sector, with the 275th Division and 2nd SS Panzer Division reacting afterwards. Relationship: First Army operated under 21st Army Group (Montgomery) until 12th Army Group became operational on 1 August.

current_activity: command post at Vouilly while Operation Cobra opens
notes: Event date: 25 July 1944 (Cobra D-day; Breakout-13 p251). Event definition: command-post location of First Army on the day Cobra opened; the Cobra attack row is C0284. Location: the army headquarters moved from Cricqueville-en-Bessin to Vouilly on 2 July and stayed until 2 August (monument text and normandie44lamemoire: site one kilometre west of the village, D5/D11 crossroads); the CMH command-post list places the army at Isigny from 5 July, which now includes Vouilly. Coordinates: village centroid, site not surveyed. Relationship: 21st Army Group had operational control of First Army until 12th Army Group became operational (1 August).

current_activity: Hodges assumes command as First Army passes to 12th Army Group
notes: Event date: Breakout-18 p343: at noon on 1 August the 12th Army Group became operational, General Hodges assumed command of First Army and Third Army came to life. Event definition: change of First Army commander (Bradley to Hodges) and of its parent headquarters (21st Army Group to 12th Army Group). Location: the Vouilly plaque and normandie44lamemoire say the army headquarters moved to Vouilly on 2 July and stayed until 2 August (a local memorial inaugurated in 2018-2019). The CMH list (World War II by Day) has Saint-Gilles from 1 August and Isigny (which includes Vouilly) from 5 July. Review (Batch 2 corrections): C0484 and C0485 were a conflict group, G015. The two sources do not exclude each other: one says the headquarters left Vouilly on 2 August, the other dates the Saint-Gilles entry to 1 August, 23 km away. They fit a move on 1-2 August, with the order of events within those two days not documented (an advance echelon, the main headquarters, or the list's arrival date convention), so G015 is dissolved and C0485 is the next headquarters location, not an alternative. This row keeps Vouilly because the plaque places the headquarters there through 1 August. Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned from 1 August; 21st Army Group control ended 31 July (C0483). Event support: high (Green Book, noon 1 August). Location support: moderate (local memorial; CMH list differs by a day and 23 km).

current_activity: headquarters moves from Vouilly to Saint-Gilles; Hodges in command
notes: Event date: CMH command-post list (World War II by Day): First Army at Saint-Gilles from 1 August (previous entry Isigny, 5 July); Breakout-18 p343 for the 1 August command change. Event definition: headquarters move from Vouilly (C0484) to Saint-Gilles. The Vouilly plaque has the headquarters there until 2 August, so the move spans 1-2 August; whether the 1 August list entry is an advance echelon, the main headquarters or an arrival-date convention is not documented. This row is in sequence with C0484, not an alternative to it (conflict group G015 dissolved, see C0484). Location: Saint-Gilles commune centroid, site not located. Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned from 1 August.

current_activity: defeating the German counterattack at Mortain with VII Corps
notes: Operation Lüttich (7 August): 2nd SS Panzer Division attacked Mortain; 30th Division held the town after occupying it on 6 August. Hodges had commanded First Army since 1 August (Breakout-18 p343). Point is the engagement sector.

current_activity: securing Paris with V Corps after the German garrison surrendered
notes: V Corps (Gerow) took responsibility for Paris; the army command post was not in the city. Point is the city, not the army HQ.

current_activity: command post near Fontenay-Trésigny, east of Paris
notes: Green Book (p671) places the First Army command post near Fontenay-Trésigny when 3rd Armored Division passed within a mile of it on 28 August.

current_activity: VII Corps seizing Mons and trapping German columns in the Mons Pocket
notes: Point is Mons (3rd Armored Division took firm possession on the morning of 3 September, Breakout-32 p681), not the army command post.

current_activity: takes VIII Corps and the Ardennes sector from Ninth Army; XIX Corps goes to Ninth
notes: Event date: 22 October 1944, noon (Siegfried p378: Bradley ordered First Army to take command of the Ninth Army's VIII Corps and its divisions and Ninth Army to take over XIX Corps; the Ninth Army was to open a command post at Maastricht on 22 October and at noon on that date the paper transfer of corps and supporting units was to take place). Event definition: First Army regains the Ardennes-Eifel sector through VIII Corps and gives up XIX Corps north of Aachen to Ninth Army; only headquarters and a few supporting troops physically move. Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned since 1 August (Breakout-18 p343). Location: First Army's headquarters was at Spa for the fall campaign (Siegfried p23) and was still at Spa on 16 December (Ardennes p330); no source used places it elsewhere on 22 October, so the place is inferred from both ends and is not documented for the date. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Spa, Belgium. Event support: high (Green Book states the order and the noon time of the paper transfer). Location support: low (Spa documented for the season and for 16 December, not for the day, so the headquarters is not tied to the date).

current_activity: headquarters moves from Spa to Chaudfontaine
notes: Event date: 19 December 1944 (Ardennes p423: Hodges' headquarters "had been moved on the 19th from Spa to Chaudfontaine"; p343 has the move done by the morning of the directive to the XVIII Airborne Corps). Event definition: army headquarters leaves Spa for Chaudfontaine as the German thrust develops (Ardennes p423 ties the move to the communications problem). Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned until the command change of 20 December. Location: Chaudfontaine commune centroid; the building is not stated. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Chaudfontaine. Event support: high (dated in the Green Book narrative). Location support: high for the commune, moderate for the site.

current_activity: passes to 21st Army Group under Montgomery
notes: Event date: 20 December 1944 (Ardennes p425: Bradley telephoned this word to First Army later in the morning; Montgomery reached Hodges' command post an hour or so after noon). The hour of effect is not documented. Event definition: First Army (with Ninth Army) is placed under Montgomery's 21st Army Group; the 12th Army Group keeps Third Army. The CMH tables show the 12th Army Group column unchanged and the British 21st Army Group in the attached column. Relationship: British 21st Army Group operational_control from 20 December (Eisenhower's order placing First and Ninth Armies under Montgomery's command); 12th Army Group assigned stays listed because the CMH tables keep it in the assigned column. The control ends on 17 January 1945 (effective_to is the inclusive last day; the tables' first row without the 21st Army Group column is 18 January); that end date is outside this batch window and is taken from the tables. Location: Chaudfontaine, the headquarters since the 19th (Ardennes p423, p426 for 20 December). Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Chaudfontaine. Event support: high (Green Book narrative and CMH tables agree). Location support: high for the commune, moderate for the site.
